In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surah al-Humazah

It is Meccan, and Allah knows best.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Woe to every slanderer and backbiter﴾. We have already explained the meaning of woe (al-waylu).

And His saying: ﴿a slanderer, a backbiter﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: al-humazah is the one who stabs at people and disparages them, and al-lumazah is the one who backbites them. Similarly from Mujahid. It was also said the reverse: al-humazah is the one who backbites, and al-lumazah is the one who stabs at people. This was stated by al-Suddi and others. And from some of them: that al-humazah is the one who harms people by tongue or hand, and al-lumazah is the one who harms them with the eyebrow (and the eye). This is a rare opinion. And from Ibn 'Abbas, in one narration: the verse was revealed concerning al-Akhnas ibn Shariq al-Zuhri. This is a well-known opinion. And they recited, regarding al-humazah and al-lumazah:

(He shows you friendliness to your face when he meets you, but if you are absent, he becomes the one who slanders and backbites you.)

Wa qawluhu: ﴿alladhi jama'a malan wa 'addadah﴾ bi-at-tashdid wa at-takhfif. Fa-qawluhu: ﴿jama'a﴾ bi-at-takhfif ma'lum, wa-bi-at-tashdid fa-al-ma'na: annahu jama'a min kulli wajhin shay'an fa-shay'an.

Wa qawluhu: ﴿wa 'addadah﴾ ay a'addahu li-nafsihi wa li-hawadithihi, wa qurii: "wa 'addadah" bi-at-takhfif, wa ma'nahu: jama'a 'adadan ay: qawman wa ansaran yataqawwa bihim.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 104, verse 3:

And His saying: ﴿He thinks that his wealth will make him immortal﴾. That is: it will remain for him forever (lit. "until its remainder"), so said al-Hasan. And some of them said: that is, it will keep death away from him.

Translation:

And His saying: ﴿Nay, he will surely be thrown into the Huţamah﴾ is one of the names of Hell. Ibn Mişraf recited: "li-yunbadhanna fi al-ḥuţamah" (he will surely be thrown into the Ḥuţamah), meaning himself and his wealth. The fire was called ḥuţamah because it consumes everything.

It is said: "a man is ḥuṭamah," meaning, one who eats much. It is also said: it is so called because it breaks everything, from al-ḥaṭm, which means breaking.
"And His saying: ﴿And what will make you know what the Crusher is?﴾ We have already explained it."

"And His saying: ﴿The fire of Allah, kindled, which mounts over the hearts﴾. It means: its pain and anguish reach the heart (al-fu'ad)."

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: The fire consumes their bodies; when the fire reaches the heart, they are restored as they were, and the fire returns to consuming them. Thus it is forever.

"And His saying: ﴿The fire of Allah, kindled, which mounts over the hearts﴾. It means: its pain and anguish reach the heart (al-fu'ad)."

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: The fire consumes their bodies; when the fire reaches the heart, they are restored as they were, and the fire returns to consuming them. Thus it is forever.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed it will be closed down upon them﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas and Abu Hurayra said: "sealed shut" (mutbaqa). It was also said: "locked" (mughlaqa).

It is said: aṣadtu al-bāb, meaning I closed the door.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 104, verse 9:

And His saying: ﴿In pillars﴾. It is also read "in extended pillars" (fi ʿamadin mumaddadah) with a fatha on the ʿayn and a raf' (nominative) on the final letter. Al-Aʿmash, Talhah and Yahya ibn Wathhab read "with extended pillars" (bi-ʿamadin mumaddah), which is the meaning of the well-known reading. It is related from some of them that the extended pillars are the shackles on their necks; from some of them, that they are the fetters on their feet; and from some of them, that they are fetters upon their graves of fire in which they are tormented. The most preferred of these opinions is that they are closed in by pillars, meaning: sealed shut, so that nothing of their pus-filled discharge comes out from it and no breath enters it.

It is related from Qatadah: they are tormented with pillars (al-ʿamad), which is the plural of ʿamud (pillar).

It is related from Abu Jaʿfar al-Qari that he once wept when this surah was recited to him. He was asked: "What makes you weep, Abu Jaʿfar?" He said: "Zayd ibn Aslam informed me that the people of the Fire do not breathe, and that is what made me weep."

And His saying: ﴿extended﴾. It is said: lengthened (mutawwalah). It is also said: stretched out (mamdudah).

Al-Naqqash mentioned in his tafsir that a man from among the believers will remain in the Fire for a thousand years, saying: "O Most Merciful, O Bestower!" while he is in one of the ravines of the Fire. Then God says to Jibril: "Bring out My servant from the Fire." Jibril, peace be upon him, comes and finds the Fire closed (mu'sadah), i.e., sealed shut. He returns and says: "O Lord, I have found the Fire sealed shut." He says: "O Jibril, go and open it and bring out My servant from the Fire." Jibril returns and brings him out, and he is like a black charred stick (khilal). He casts him on the shore of Paradise until God causes hair, flesh and blood to grow on him, and admits him into Paradise.

He narrated it from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, and he mentioned that the Fire closes over them so that they despair of coming out of it. And God knows best.
